label: ASRS v1.1 (Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale)
summary: 18-item WHO-developed screener. Part A (6 items, cutoff ≥4) determines the screen; Part B (12 items) characterises symptom load. Deliberately tuned for sensitivity, so a positive screen is a reason to evaluate, not a diagnosis.

label: Cognitive Trade-off Task (ASRT + Go/No-Go)
summary: The paradigm used by Horváth et al. 2026: an Alternating Serial Reaction Time Task carrying a hidden probabilistic sequence (statistical learning) with an embedded Go/No-Go component (response inhibition), so both are measured at once rather than in isolation.

label: Continuous performance test (CPT / QbTest)
summary: Sustained-attention task requiring responses to targets and withholding to non-targets over a long, monotonous session. Indexes vigilance, inhibition and reaction-time variability; sensitive to ADHD but not diagnostically specific.

label: Stop-signal / go-no-go task
summary: Measures the ability to cancel an already-initiated response (the stop-signal reaction time) — the cleanest isolation of response inhibition.

label: Delay-discounting / choice-delay task
summary: Choices between smaller-sooner and larger-later rewards, quantifying how steeply delayed value is discounted — the motivational/delay-aversion pathway.

label: Working-memory task (n-back / span)
summary: n-back and complex-span paradigms indexing the capacity to hold and manipulate information over short intervals.

label: SWAN rating scale
summary: Strengths and Weaknesses of ADHD-symptoms and Normal-behavior scale: rates each symptom on a symmetric −3 to +3 range so both tails are measured, yielding roughly normally distributed population scores.

label: CAARS (Conners Adult ADHD Rating Scales)
summary: Norm-referenced adult ADHD rating scale scored as T-scores against a population sample; the T≥65 cutoff trades sensitivity for specificity.

label: BAARS-IV (Barkley Adult ADHD Rating Scale)
summary: DSM-anchored adult ADHD rating scale with current and childhood-symptom subscales, self- or observer-administered.

label: PID-5 (Disinhibition domain)
summary: Dimensional maladaptive-trait inventory; its Disinhibition domain (and Distractibility facet) places a person on the HiTOP disinhibited-externalizing spectrum rather than in the ADHD category.

label: Internal Restlessness Scale (IRS)
summary: Self-report scale (Weyandt et al., 2003) that operationalises the subjective/mental restlessness adults with ADHD report in place of overt motor hyperactivity; four factors — internal distractibility, internal impulsivity, internal restlessness, internal disorganization.
